Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) Refuses to Accept Money Given to him

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen narrates that a chief of a rural area of Iraq once requested Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) to ask (Ameerul Mu'mineen) Hadhrat Ali (RA) to address a need he had. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) therefore interceded on his behalf and Hadhrat Ali (RA) acceded to the request. The chief then sent forty thousand Dirhams to the Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) with the message that it was from him. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) returned the money with the message, "We do not sell our good deeds."[^2]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Arqam (RA) Refuses to Accept Money Given to him

Hadhrat Amr bin Dinaar narrates that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) appointed Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Arqam (RA) as treasurer of the Baytul Maal. When Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) gave him three hundred thousand as remuneration, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Arqam (RA) refused to accept the money. The rest of the narration is the same as the narration of Imaam Maalik, which states that when Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) gave Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Arqam (RA) thirty thousand as remuneration, he refused to take the money saying, "I did it for the pleasure of Allaah."[^3]
Hadhrat Amr bin Nu'maan bin Muqarrin (RA) Refuses to Accept Money Given to him
The Incident with Mus'Ab bin Zubayr

Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Qurra reports that he was once staying with Hadhrat Amr bin Nu'maan bin Muqarrin (RA). When Ramadhaan arrived, someone came with a bag of Dirhams saying, "The Ameer Mus'ab bin Zubayr conveys his Salaams and says that his gifts shall reach every Qaari (and you are one of them). Please use this money." Hadhrat Amr bin Nu'maan (RA) said (to the messenger), "Tell him that we swear by Allaah that we do not recite the Qur'aan with the intention of earning worldly profits." He then sent the money back.[^4]
